Table of Contents: Extended Data 1. Summary of 89 genome-wide association study (GWAS) phenotypes in the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES) cohorts.
Extended Data1: Extendeds Data 1. Summary of 89 genome-wide association study (GWAS) phenotypes in the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES) cohorts. This dataset provides an overview of phenotype definitions and sample characteristics for all traits included in the GWAS analyses. Disease endpoints are summarized as case–control counts, while clinical biomarkers measured at baseline are summarized using descriptive statistics. For each phenotype, values are reported for both the total KoGES population (N = 211,562) and the GWAS analytic sample after quality control (N = 152,719). For binary traits, case and control counts, case–control ratios, and the number of missing observations (NA) are provided. For continuous traits, summary statistics include sample size, mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, and the number of missing observations (NA). Phenotype definitions and measurement units are provided in the corresponding columns. NA indicates missing or unavailable data.
Extended Data2A: Extendeds Data 2A. Genome-wide significant continuous trait associations identified in Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES) with cross-cohort novelty classification and external replication results. Each row represents one phenotype–lead variant association identified in the KoGES GWAS. Novelty was assessed by comparing each lead variant against external summary statistics from East Asian cohorts (BBJ, TWB, and TPMI), European cohorts (UK Biobank, FinnGen, and MVP), and the NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog; a locus was considered previously reported if a genome-wide significant association (P < 5×10⁻⁸) was present within ±1 Mb. External replication was assessed at the panel level by inverse-variance weighted (IVW) fixed-effects meta-analysis across contributing cohorts within each panel. A variant was classified as replicated if the IVW meta-analysis p-value fell below the Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold (EAS: p < 8.10×10⁻⁶; EUR: p < 9.94×10⁻⁶) and the effect direction was concordant with the KoGES discovery effect. "Not analyzed" indicates that no matching summary statistics were available for that variant in the corresponding cohort or panel. Rows are sorted by phenotype and chromosomal position.

Extended Data3: Extendeds Data 3. Conditionally independent genome-wide significant associations identified after conditioning on previously reported East Asian signals within Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES). Shown are 172 KoGES lead associations that remained genome-wide significant (P < 5×10⁻⁸) after conditioning on all clump-defined prior signals from external East Asian cohorts (BBJ, TWB, and TPMI) within ±1 Mb. Marginal statistics are from the original KoGES GWAS. Conditional statistics were obtained using GCTA-COJO (--cojo-cond) with KoGES individual-level genotype data as the LD reference. "n condition SNPs requested" indicates the number of conditioning variants defined by source-stratified clumping; "Condition SNPs retained by GCTA" indicates those present in the KoGES dataset and used in the final conditioning model.
Extended Data4A: Extended Data 4A. East Asian panel meta-analysis replication results for continuous trait associations identified in Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES). Each row represents one phenotype–lead variant association identified in the KoGES GWAS. Panel-level replication statistics were obtained by inverse-variance weighted (IVW) fixed-effects meta-analysis across all contributing cohorts within each panel. A variant was classified as replicated if the IVW meta-analysis p-value fell below the Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold and the effect direction was concordant with the KoGES discovery effect. Per-cohort direction pattern indicates whether all, some, or none of the contributing cohorts showed effects in the same direction as KoGES. Between-cohort heterogeneity was quantified using the I² statistic and Cochran Q test for variants with summary statistics available from two or more cohorts.

Extended Data6A: Extendeds Data 6A. Winner's curse corrected effect estimates for genome-wide significant continuous trait phenotype–lead variant associations identified in the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES). Winner's curse correction was applied to account for the upward bias in effect size estimates arising from selection of lead variants at genome-wide significance. For each phenotype–lead variant association, the winner's curse corrected beta (β_WC) was estimated by maximizing the conditional likelihood of the observed discovery Z-statistic given that it exceeded the genome-wide significance threshold (|Z| >= 5.45, corresponding to P < 5×10⁻⁸). The corrected effect estimate was obtained as (Winner's curse corrected beta) = (raw beta) × (θ_WC / |Z_raw|), where θ_WC is the maximum likelihood estimate of the true effect size under the conditional distribution. The shrinkage ratio (|β_WC / β_raw|) quantifies the degree of correction, with values closer to 1 indicating minimal winner's curse attenuation and values closer to 0 indicating substantial downward correction. KoGES beta and standard error are the original discovery-stage estimates. Rows are sorted by phenotype and chromosomal position.
Extended Data6B: Extendeds Data 6B. Winner's curse corrected effect estimates for genome-wide significant binary trait phenotype–lead variant associations identified in the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES). Winner's curse correction was applied to account for the upward bias in effect size estimates arising from selection of lead variants at genome-wide significance. For each phenotype–lead variant association, the winner's curse corrected beta (β_WC) was estimated by maximizing the conditional likelihood of the observed discovery Z-statistic given that it exceeded the genome-wide significance threshold (|Z| >= 5.45, corresponding to P < 5×10⁻⁸). For binary traits, the discovery Z-statistic was derived from SAIGE-based p-values. The corrected effect estimate was obtained as β_WC = β_raw × (θ_WC / |Z_raw|), where θ_WC is the maximum likelihood estimate of the true effect size under the conditional distribution. The shrinkage ratio (|β_WC / β_raw|) quantifies the degree of correction, with values closer to 1 indicating minimal winner's curse attenuation and values closer to 0 indicating substantial downward correction. KoGES beta and standard error are the original discovery-stage estimates. Rows are sorted by phenotype and chromosomal position.
